chapters.title: How Microsoft platforms created shadow IT

takeaways: Foundry agents are autonomous workloads under non-human identities, so every agent needs a dedicated workload identity with an owner, a purpose, an expiry and a shutdown trigger.
Shared service principals and convenience exceptions cause permission drift, and per-system Purview and DLP rules miss data combinations an agent assembles across systems.
Governance must act before execution: no owner, no label and no audit path means no production deployment for an agent.
hook: Microsoft Foundry makes it easy to build agents that run on schedules and events with no human in the loop, which is how shadow IT turns autonomous. This episode is for identity, compliance and platform governance owners who need to control Foundry before the first incident. You get three failure modes, an agent control plane built on identity, Purview labels and observability, and a week-one checklist.
